parts.latex:
Which calculation should be used to find the value of $x$ in $\triangle PQR$ ?

\exfigure{2843_q3a_1}

solutions.latex:
Two angles and their opposite sides are involved, so use the sine rule. The side opposite $x^\circ$ is 12 and the side opposite $120^\circ$ is 20.
$$\dfrac{\sin x^\circ}{12} = \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{20}$$
Hence the answer is option B.

solution sketch: Triangle with angle B = 46 degrees marked

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{3296_q7b_s1}

Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ABC &= 180^\circ-87^\circ-47^\circ \\ &= 46^\circ \end{aligned}$$
By the sine rule in triangle ABC:
$$\dfrac{AC}{\sin 46^\circ} = \dfrac{230}{\sin 47^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} AC &= \dfrac{230\sin 46^\circ}{\sin 47^\circ} \\ &\approx 226.22 \text{ m (2 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$

figures.cap: triangle ABC with AB = 54 km, BC = 51 km and bearings 215 and 349
solution sketch: bearing diagram annotated with 35 and 11 degree angles

parts.latex:
While they were constructing the plant, they planned to connect the plant to substations in several towns in the local area with power lines.

A surveyor is sent to survey each route to help determine the cost of constructing each possible route.

As part of his journey, he travelled from Nyngan ($A$) to Nevertire ($B$) and then to Tottenham ($C$).

The bearing of Tottenham from Nevertire is $215^\circ$, and the bearing of Nyngan from Tottenham is $349^\circ$. This is shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{2841_q6_1}

Find the size of angle $\angle ABC$, correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{2841_q6_s1}

In the diagram, $\angle ACB = 11^\circ + 35^\circ = 46^\circ$.

Let $\alpha = \angle BAC$. Using the sine rule in triangle $ABC$:
$$\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{51} = \dfrac{\sin 46^\circ}{54}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \sin\alpha &= \dfrac{51\sin 46^\circ}{54} \\ \alpha &= \sin^{-1}(\text{Ans}) \\ &= 42.7949\ldots \\ &\approx 43^\circ \end{aligned}$$
The angle sum of a triangle is $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ABC &= 180^\circ - 43^\circ - 46^\circ \\ &= 91^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle ABC = 91^\circ$$
criteria: Finds the angle at $A$ ($43^\circ$), or equivalent merit
Writes the correct sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with sides 5, 4, 8 and angle 122.6 degrees

parts.latex:
\exfigure{706_q4_1}

For the triangle shown above, the value of $\sin\theta^\circ$ is given by:

solutions.latex:
The angle $122.6^\circ$ lies between the sides $5$ and $4$, so it is opposite the side $8$. The angle $\theta$ is opposite the side $4$.

Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{4} = \dfrac{\sin 122.6^\circ}{8}$$
$$\sin\theta = \dfrac{4\sin 122.6^\circ}{8} = \dfrac{\sin 122.6^\circ}{2}$$
The cosine rule would not give this expression, so D fails.

figures.cap: triangle with angle 23°37', sides 54.1 cm and 25 cm, obtuse angle theta

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule in the triangle:
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{54.1} = \dfrac{\sin 23^\circ 37'}{25}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \sin\theta &= \dfrac{54.1 \times \sin 23^\circ 37'}{25} \\ \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{54.1 \times \sin 23^\circ 37'}{25}\right) \\ &= 60^\circ 6' 15'' \end{aligned}$$
Since $\theta$ is obtuse:
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= 180^\circ - 60^\circ 6' 15'' \\ &= 119^\circ 53' 45'' \\ &\approx 119^\circ 54' \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta \approx 119^\circ 54'$$
criteria: Finds the acute angle $60^\circ 6'$, or equivalent merit
Substitutes correctly into the sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with sides 21 m, x m, 29 m and angles 61 and 40 degrees

parts.latex:
\exfigure{3295_q4_1}

What is the correct expression for $x$?

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule, with $x$ opposite $61^\circ$ and $29$ opposite $79^\circ$:
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 61^\circ} = \dfrac{29}{\sin 79^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{29}{\sin 79^\circ} \times \sin 61^\circ \\ &= \dfrac{29\sin 61^\circ}{\sin 79^\circ} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is C.
